info.title: mocker admin API
info.description:
The admin plane of mocker: everything the web UI talks to.

This document is the CONTRACT, not documentation-after-the-fact. web/ generates its
entire API client from it (orval), and internal/admin/openapi_contract_test.go fails
the Go build's test bar if a single (method, path) here disagrees with the routes
internal/admin actually registers. Adding a handler without adding it here — or the
reverse — is a red test, not a silent drift.

Every route below is served on the admin host (MOCKER_ADMIN_HOST) only. The mock
plane (per-workspace hosts) is a different surface entirely and is NOT described here.

servers.description: Same origin as the UI: the SPA is served by this very binary, so the client never needs an absolute base URL.

tags.name: auth
tags.description: Session login/logout and the current session's identity.

tags.name: operations
tags.description: Spec operations as merged with a workspace's overrides, and the override editor.

tags.name: endpoints
tags.description: Custom endpoints: routes a workspace serves that no spec declares.

tags.name: traffic
tags.description: The recorded request log, and the two conversions from a recorded row.

tags.name: session
tags.description: Live-state directives: force a status, fail N times.

tags.name: scenarios
tags.description: DESIGN §4's Scenario layer (P2b): named snapshots of a workspace's settings and op_overrides rows, composed at request time over the workspace's own layer, never restored over it.

tags.name: checkpoints
tags.description: P2c: history and undo for the workspace layer (DESIGN §12:759-776). A checkpoint is a point in a workspace's history, distinct from a scenario (P2b): rolling back WRITES the snapshot's settings and endpoints back wholesale, upserts its confirmed-family configuration without ever deleting a row (P3b), and allocates a new revision, rather than composing over them at serve time.

tags.name: resources
tags.description: Route families derived from a spec (a collection route and its detail route, with no path parameter inside the collection segment itself), confirmed or declined per workspace, and served out of SQLite once confirmed (DESIGN §11, §19). Three routes, not the CRUD table DESIGN §14 originally named for this surface: a resource id does not exist before a confirm, so there is nothing for a REST-shaped DELETE/PUT pair to address, and the single decision route (confirm or decline) absorbs both transitions instead.

tags.name: drift
tags.description: P4a (decisions.md mocker-p4a-triage): the three things that silently stop working when a workspace is re-bound to a new spec version or a rederive drops a family — an orphaned operation override, an orphaned confirmed resource family, a custom endpoint shadowing a spec operation. Read-only: every repair already has its own verb elsewhere.

tags.name: stream
tags.description: P6a: the process-wide health of the SSE traffic feed. The feed itself is under `traffic`.

sessionCookie.name: mocker_session
sessionCookie.description: Set by POST /api/auth/login. HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, and Secure unless MOCKER_DEV=1.

csrfToken.name: X-CSRF-Token
csrfToken.description: Required on every POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE except login. Value comes from the login/me response's csrfToken. Compared in constant time. Two further checks apply to the same requests and are NOT expressible here: Content-Type must parse to exactly application/json, and Origin (or Referer, when Origin is absent) must have hostname == MOCKER_ADMIN_HOST.

opKey.name: opKey
opKey.description: Already percent-encoded (url.PathEscape of "METHOD path", e.g. GET%20%2Fpets%2F%7BpetId%7D). Pass this value VERBATIM as the {opKey} path segment — re-encoding it (e.g. with encodeURIComponent) double-encodes the leading %25 and breaks the lookup.

connectionId.name: cid
connectionId.description: A live connection id from GET .../connections. Issued by the running process, valid only while it runs: after a restart the same number can name a different connection. Positive decimal int64; anything else answers 400.

assetName.name: name
assetName.description: The asset's name: one path segment of [A-Za-z0-9._-], at most 128 characters. Addressed by name, never by id (DESIGN §32.3): a name survives delete-and-reupload.

BadRequest.description: Malformed request: unparseable body, an out-of-range field, an invalid path parameter.

Unauthorized.description: No session, or an expired one. The UI treats this on any non-login call as "the session died" and returns to the login screen.

Forbidden.description: CSRF refusal: a missing/incorrect X-CSRF-Token, or an Origin/Referer whose hostname is not MOCKER_ADMIN_HOST.

NotFound.description: The addressed resource does not exist.

Conflict.description: The request is well-formed and the resource exists, but the operation is not legitimate in this state.

UnsupportedMediaType.description: Content-Type did not parse to application/json.

Internal.description: Server-side failure. The message is deliberately generic; the detail is in the server log.

ServiceUnavailable.description: A dependency this route needs was never wired into the server (live state, traffic recorder).

Error.description: The single error envelope every non-2xx answer on this plane uses (internal/httpx/respond.go).

code.description: Stable machine code. The shared set is bad_request, unauthorized, forbidden, not_found, conflict, too_large, internal; session's GET/POST/DELETE add service_unavailable (no LiveStateSource wired in this deployment), and login adds rate_limited and unsupported_media_type. not_implemented_yet does not appear anywhere in this contract: it named DESIGN §12's scenario switch before scenarios existed (POST .../session {"scenario":...} answered 501), and stopped being true the moment scenarios shipped their own activate/deactivate routes (A17) — that key is a plain 400 here now. A3 adds edit_conflict on the five per-row compare-and-swap routes (PATCH /api/workspaces/{id}, PUT .../operations/{opKey}, POST .../auth-preset, PUT .../endpoints/{eid}, PUT .../scenarios/{sid}): the caller's editVersion expectation no longer matches the row's stored edit_version.

message.description: Human text. Shown to the operator as-is.

details.description: Per-field validation detail. Absent unless the route produces one.

name.description: Trimmed, non-empty, no control characters, at most 64 runes — enforced server-side. A UI that pre-validates must use exactly these rules and no others.

ScenarioActiveView.description: Answered by both activate and deactivate.

scenarioId.description: null after a successful deactivate, or after activating a scenario that was already active (A7: idempotent — same value, same revision, no write at all).

revision.description: The workspace's revision AFTER this call. Unchanged from before the call when the target was already active/inactive (A7).

ScenarioDetailView.description: The full decoded snapshot — deliberately NOT the list shape (see ScenarioListView): this is what screen 5's active-scenario banner reads to learn which settings/overrides keys a running scenario currently masks. GET .../operations/{opKey} is never composed with an active scenario (A18), so this route is the only place that view is visible at all.

basePath.description: Duplicates settings.basePath (the bundle format's own A14 rule). Never actually composed from a scenario snapshot when it is active — the WORKSPACE's own basePath is what a route table is always built from, so a scenario snapshotted at another prefix cannot silently relocate every route.

editVersion.description: A3's per-row compare-and-swap token for the scenarios row: the value to send back as PUT .../scenarios/{sid}'s editVersion. Both this read and that write's response share this schema, so a caller can write twice without re-reading between them.

ScenarioOverrideEntry.description: One op_overrides row as stored inside the snapshot (the bundle encodes ROWS, never merge intent — a key absent from a scenario's overrides array falls through to the workspace's own row for that operation; a key present with overrideOn:false means the scenario deliberately masks the workspace's edit back to the spec's own answer, a third state distinct from either). Reuses PUT .../operations/{opKey}'s own OverrideMutableFields shape, with method/path added since a snapshot entry is not scoped to one URL segment the way that route's own path parameter is.

failDirective.description: Arbitrary JSON. Preserved only — this slice's serving path does not interpret it.

ScenarioSpecRefView.description: The spec identity this snapshot was taken against, for PROVENANCE ONLY — never consulted by the server to decide whether the snapshot may be used. A row for a route the current spec no longer has is simply inert, never an error.

hash.description: Bare hex sha256 of the spec document — no "sha256:" scheme prefix.

inline.description: Arbitrary JSON. Always null in this slice — reserved for a future portable export/import that travels without a server-side spec row to point hash/name at.

ScenarioSummaryView.description: One entry of the scenario list — never the snapshot itself: a list that answered every scenario's full snapshot would be a page-load cost that grows with the workspace's history, for a screen that only ever shows a name, a date and which one is active. Fetch GET .../scenarios/{sid} for the snapshot.

editVersion.description: A3's per-row compare-and-swap token for this scenarios row.

ServerConfigView.description: Server-side configuration the browser cannot derive on its own. MOCKER_ADMIN_HOST is forbidden from sitting under MOCKER_BASE_DOMAIN, so window.location tells the UI nothing about either the base domain or the reserved prefix.

reservedPrefix.description: MOCKER_RESERVED_PREFIX — the path prefix a workspace's mock plane answers its own control routes on ({prefix}/health, {prefix}/state). Never hard-code /__mocker in the UI: it is configurable and the acceptance run uses a different value on purpose.

baseDomain.description: MOCKER_BASE_DOMAIN — the domain workspace hosts live under in host routing mode.

limits.description: A9: the effective ceilings of this process, the same config.Limits an agent reads through get_server_config. Bytes are bytes, seconds are seconds.

maxResponseBytes.description: MOCKER_MAX_RESPONSE — a body, and one stream frame

streamTrafficFrames.description: MOCKER_STREAM_TRAFFIC_FRAMES — off | first | all (A14: every frame each way into the connection's one row, under the two budgets below)

streamTrafficMaxFrames.description: MOCKER_STREAM_TRAFFIC_MAX_FRAMES — frames per row each way under "all"

streamTrafficMaxBytes.description: MOCKER_STREAM_TRAFFIC_MAX_BYTES — bytes per row each way under "all"

data.description: The row as a JSON object. data[idField] is overwritten with the key.

scopeKey.description: A nested family's outer parameter tuple, encoded as resources.EncodeScope does (values url.PathEscape'd and joined with /). Default "", the top-level scope. Not verified against live ancestor rows: a row placed under an unanchored scope is unreachable until one exists.

baseScopeKey.description: The declared basePath-parameter value tuple, for a workspace whose basePath carries a parameter. Default "".

DeleteResourceEntityRequest.description: DELETE .../resources/{family}/entities/{key}'s optional body (A11): the scope the key is addressed under.

created.description: true when the call inserted the row, false when it replaced one.

AuthResponse.description: The shared answer of POST /api/auth/login and GET /api/me.

csrfToken.description: Send back as X-CSRF-Token on every state-changing call.

Identity.description: The synthetic user a workspace's generated responses and minted tokens describe.

id.description: Any JSON scalar — specs disagree about whether a user id is a number or a string.

Settings.description: A workspace's generation and behaviour knobs (internal/domain).

seed.description: Deterministic generation seed: the same seed and the same spec produce byte-identical bodies.

basePathValues.description: Declares which values basePath's {param} segments may take (P3h). Each element is one base TUPLE: the k raw values a {param}-carrying basePath declares, joined with "/" in the order the parameters appear in basePath — an element must split on "/" into exactly k non-empty components, so for one parameter that reduces to "no / at all", and for two it is e.g. "7/eu". Omitted or empty when basePath carries no parameter, which is every workspace before this field existed. A request whose base value is not one of these is refused with 404 entity_not_found on every resource-served route before storage is touched; nothing populates a value that is not declared here.

notFoundBody.description: Arbitrary JSON served as the workspace's 404 body. Absent when unset.

revision.description: Bumped by every write that the mock plane must notice. The UI uses it as a cheap "did anything change" signal.

url.description: This workspace's externally reachable mock-plane origin. NO base path, NO trailing slash, port carried from the request Host. Built server-side because nothing lets a browser derive it: /api/me carries no host information and the admin host may not sit under the base domain.

editVersion.description: A3's per-row compare-and-swap token for this workspaces row — distinct from revision above, which is cache-invalidation bookkeeping and is never bumped by fields PATCH cannot write. This view is shared by every route that answers a workspace (list, create, get, patch), so all four carry it, and PATCH's write response shares this schema too: a caller can write twice without re-reading between them.

CreateScenarioRequest.description: Snapshots the workspace's CURRENT settings and op_overrides rows into a new named scenario (there is no scenario editor — a scenario's contents can only be produced by putting the workspace into that state and snapshotting it). Refused with 409 while another scenario is already active for this workspace and from is absent (deactivate it first, or pass from to clone instead).

from.description: Id of a scenario already saved in this same workspace. When present, the new scenario's snapshot is a clone of THAT scenario's stored snapshot rather than a snapshot of the workspace's current layer, and its presence bypasses the 409 refusal that otherwise applies while a scenario is active for this workspace. The clone never reads the workspace's own layer, so the coherent-read retry (A11) does not apply to it either — a name collision with an existing scenario in this workspace still answers 409.

RenameScenarioRequest.description: Body of PUT .../scenarios/{sid}. Changes the scenario's name and nothing else — the stored snapshot, its created_at and whether it is the workspace's active scenario are untouched.

name.description: Trimmed and validated through the same rule the create path uses; a blank or already-taken name is rejected rather than silently coerced.

editVersion.description: A3's REQUIRED compare-and-swap expectation: the scenarios row's edit_version as of the caller's last read (ScenarioDetailView.editVersion or ScenarioSummaryView.editVersion). An omitted field is rejected with 400 — a scenario addressed by {sid} always already exists, so 0 ("I expect no row") is meaningful only for the operation PUT and is refused here with 409 edit_conflict rather than accepted.

PatchWorkspaceRequest.description: name, settings and specId are all optional; an omitted one is left untouched. editVersion is the exception (A3): REQUIRED even though every other field is not.

specId.description: Attach this spec. NOT nullable: the handler decodes into a *int64, so an explicit null is indistinguishable from an omitted field and both mean "leave the current spec alone" — detaching a spec is not expressible through this route today.

editVersion.description: A3's REQUIRED compare-and-swap expectation: the workspace's edit_version as of the caller's last read (WorkspaceView.editVersion). An omitted field is rejected with 400, never treated as "no expectation" — that state exists only at workspaces.Repo's own unguarded Update verb, never on this wire.

hash.description: Content hash. Re-importing the same bytes is a no-op that returns the existing spec with duplicate: true.

pointer.description: JSON pointer into the imported document.

ReportView.description: What the importer made of a document: how much it understood, and what it had to degrade.

degraded.description: Operations that parsed but lost fidelity. A non-zero value is worth showing.

duplicate.description: true (with 200 rather than 201) when the same bytes were already imported.

document.description: The whole OpenAPI/Swagger document, as text.

OperationView.description: One operation as the importer stored it — the spec's own view, before any workspace override.

canonicalPath.description: Path with parameter names normalised, so two specs that differ only in parameter naming compare equal.

sourceOrder.description: Position in the source document. Sorting by it shows operations in the order their author wrote them.

parseError.description: Non-null when this operation was stored but could not be fully understood.

Condition.description: One clause of a variant's `when`. All clauses must match for the variant to be chosen.

Recipe.description: A generator bound to a data path: what to put there instead of a schema-derived value.

value.description: Arbitrary JSON, meaning depends on kind.

Variant.description: One response variant of an operation, keyed by status selector.

mode.description: generated: build the body from the schema. pinned: serve `body` verbatim.

body.description: Arbitrary JSON. Only meaningful when mode is pinned.

bodyRef.description: A6 (DESIGN §32.3): "asset:<name>" — on a pinned variant the body IS this workspace's uploaded asset, served verbatim under the asset's own stored media type (and X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff). Exclusive with body, bodyEncoding AND mediaType, all refused beside it; requires mode "pinned". Existence is not checked at write time: a missing asset answers the variant's status with an empty body and asset_missing in the traffic row (Preview: noBody with notes).

schemaPatch.description: Applied to the generated body of a spec operation's variant (an RFC 6902 subset: add, remove, replace). Preserved but never applied on a custom endpoint's variant — that serves a literal body, so there is nothing to patch.

schema.description: P7a (DESIGN §34.3): an inline JSON Schema a CUSTOM endpoint's generated response is walked from — a `$ref` into the bound spec's components is allowed and must resolve at write time (400 schema_ref_unresolved otherwise; with no spec bound any $ref is refused). Refused BY NAME on a spec operation's override (400 schema_on_override): that operation already has a schema — change it with schemaPatch. With a pinned body beside it the pinned body serves (§8's mode rule) and the schema only declares the exported shape.

function.description: Lua source that PRODUCES this response instead of one being assembled for it (A18). The stored string IS the function body over one argument `req`; it returns `status, body, headers`. Exclusive per variant with body, bodyEncoding, bodyRef, recipes, schemaPatch and mediaType — a variant carrying two of them is refused by name at write time, so there is no precedence to document. `when[]` is allowed: selection is unchanged and the function runs only when its variant is selected. Refused by name on a spec-operation override row (400 schema_on_override's sibling, 400 function_and_body for the pairs) and on a stream row (400 function_on_stream); a stream's Lua goes in stream.tick.lua or stream.onFrame instead. Compiled at write time: unparseable source is 400 and carries the parser's own words.

selector.description: The spec's own response key: a status, a wildcard like 2XX, or `default`.

hasSchemaPatch.description: P7b: whether this status's variant carries a schemaPatch — the «Контракт» tab's «изменено» signal, beside mode = pinned. The patch itself is only on GET .../operations/{opKey}.

OpOverrideSummaryView.description: What the list screen needs to know about an override without fetching the whole document.

routeOff.description: The operation is switched off entirely: the mock plane stops answering it.

editVersion.description: A3's per-row compare-and-swap token for this op_overrides row (D5). This object as a whole is only present when the operation has an override row at all; when present, this field is always here too.

MergedOperationView.description: A spec operation as it will actually behave in this workspace: the spec's statuses plus whatever override sits on top.

opKey.description: Already percent-encoded (url.PathEscape of "METHOD path", e.g. GET%20%2Fpets%2F%7BpetId%7D). Use this value VERBATIM as the {opKey} path segment in the operations/{opKey} routes below — re-encoding it (e.g. with encodeURIComponent) double-encodes the leading %25 and breaks the lookup.

OverrideMutableFields.description: Exactly the fields PUT accepts. Anything else in the document is server-owned.

editVersion.description: A3's per-row compare-and-swap token for this op_overrides row (D5): the value to send back as PUT .../operations/{opKey}'s editVersion. Both GET's detail read and PUT's write response (OverridePutView) embed this view, so a caller can write twice without re-reading between them.

PutOperationRequest.description: Body of PUT .../operations/{opKey}. The route's request body was a bare $ref to OverrideMutableFields before A3; that document has no wrapper of its own to carry a sibling field, so this is the one genuinely new schema A3 adds rather than extending an existing one — it composes the untouched OverrideMutableFields with editVersion beside it, never inside it (A3's own sibling rule: OverrideMutableFields is also embedded in PreviewRequest's draft, unaffected by this route).

editVersion.description: A3's REQUIRED compare-and-swap expectation: the op_overrides row's edit_version as of the caller's last read (OverrideDocView.editVersion, or 0 when GET .../operations/{opKey} answered 404 — the absent-row expectation). An omitted field is rejected with 400, never treated as "no expectation" — that state exists only at overrides.Repo's own unguarded Put verb, never on this wire. Unlike the other three single-object routes, 0 is legal here even when a row already exists at a version other than 0: op_overrides is the one table in this population where the FIRST write is an upsert from nothing, so "I expect no row yet" is a meaningful, distinct expectation.

OverrideConflictDetails.description: PUT .../operations/{opKey}'s conflict payload (A3/D6): every field PutOperationRequest accepts, as the server currently holds it — round-trippable, a caller can resend this exact document with editVersion swapped in as its new expectation and have the retry succeed.

editVersion.description: The version the server actually holds right now.

EditConflictTombstone.description: A3/D6's tombstone: the target row was deleted between the caller's read and its write, so there is no current document to hand back — only the fact and an explicitly null editVersion. Reachable on all five A3 routes' 409 except POST .../auth-preset, whose set-valued conflict (staleVersions) carries the same meaning per-entry instead (see PresetConflictDetails).

editVersion.description: Always null. The null itself is the whole message — there is no version to report because the row is gone, and this is the one place on this route's wire where editVersion is ever null rather than a plain integer.

WorkspaceConflictDetails.description: PATCH /api/workspaces/{id}'s conflict payload (A3/D6): every field PatchWorkspaceRequest accepts, as the server currently holds it — name and settings as plain values (a stored row has nothing to omit), plus the version the server actually holds.

specId.description: Nullable here, unlike PatchWorkspaceRequest's own specId: this field carries the CURRENT stored value, and a workspace genuinely attached to no spec is a real state that must round-trip as null rather than being indistinguishable from an omitted field. (See PATCH's own specId note for why the request side cannot make the same distinction.)

editVersion.description: The version the server actually holds right now.

OverrideEditConflict.description: PUT .../operations/{opKey}'s 409 envelope: the same error shape every route on this plane uses, with details given its actual per-route type here (edit_conflict only — this route answered no 409 before A3).

WorkspaceEditConflict.description: PATCH /api/workspaces/{id}'s 409 envelope: the same error shape every route on this plane uses, with details given its actual per-route type here (edit_conflict only — this route answered no 409 before A3).

EndpointConflictDetails.description: PUT .../endpoints/{eid}'s conflict payload (A3/D6): every field UpdateEndpointRequest accepts, as the server currently holds it — overrideOn/routeOff as plain bool rather than *bool, since a stored row has no "omitted" state to preserve — plus the version the server actually holds.

kind.description: P6e: the row's kind, so a stream row's conflict document is complete.

editVersion.description: The version the server actually holds right now.

reqSchema.description: P7a: the request body schema, exported as requestBody. Validated on write (shape, size, $refs); still never enforced on a request — that is P2.

EndpointEditConflict.description: The edit_conflict branch of PUT .../endpoints/{eid}'s 409 (A3/D6) — one member of EndpointPutConflict's oneOf, told apart from the pre-existing duplicate-path branch (Error, code conflict) by error.code.

EndpointPutConflict.description: PUT .../endpoints/{eid}'s full 409 shape (A3): a duplicate-path refusal (the pre-existing shared Error envelope, code conflict — #/components/responses/Conflict is deliberately left untouched, still referenced by six other routes) or an edit_conflict refusal (EndpointEditConflict, new in A3), told apart by error.code.

ScenarioConflictDetails.description: PUT .../scenarios/{sid}'s conflict payload (A3/D6): every field RenameScenarioRequest accepts — just name, since a rename changes one column — plus the version the server actually holds.

editVersion.description: The version the server actually holds right now.

ScenarioEditConflict.description: The edit_conflict branch of PUT .../scenarios/{sid}'s 409 (A3/D6) — one member of ScenarioPutConflict's oneOf, told apart from the pre-existing duplicate-name branch (Error, code conflict) by error.code.

ScenarioPutConflict.description: PUT .../scenarios/{sid}'s full 409 shape (A3): a duplicate-name refusal (the pre-existing inline Error-typed envelope, code conflict, unchanged) or an edit_conflict refusal (ScenarioEditConflict, new in A3), told apart by error.code.

PresetConflictDetails.description: D12's set-valued conflict payload for POST .../auth-preset: keyed by ONLY the opKeys that disagreed — never the whole table. NOT editVersions: a different name, a different Go type (map values may be null), and it appears only in a 409 — conflating the two would force the request/response editVersions map to accept nulls it must reject.

staleVersions.description: opKey -> the row's current edit_version, or null when that row is gone. The contrast that matters is null versus NO ENTRY: an absent opKey did not disagree and needs nothing from the caller.

PresetEditConflict.description: POST .../auth-preset's 409 envelope (A3/D6/D12): the same error shape every route on this plane uses, with details fixed to PresetConflictDetails — the single-row EditConflictTombstone is not a shape this route may answer; a preset row deleted meanwhile is reported inline in staleVersions as a null entry instead.

revision.description: The workspace revision after this write.

Binding.description: One proposed recipe binding: a place in a response that should be a minted token/identity value rather than a generated one.

reason.description: Human text explaining why this was proposed.

AuthPresetProposal.description: What the preset WOULD write. GET produces it and writes nothing; POST applies the operator-approved subset. GET also gains a ForWorkspace read for editVersions below (A3, D5/D8) — new as of A3, but the route stays read-only.

notes.description: What was skipped and why — a silent skip reads as "nothing to do".

sampleJwt.description: One minted token, so the operator sees what will actually be served.

editVersions.description: A3's per-row compare-and-swap tokens, one entry per opKey the bindings above resolve to (never per binding — two bindings on one operation still collapse to the one op_overrides row they'd both write). 0 means that opKey has no override row yet (D7's absent-row expectation), never an absent entry — the map covers EXACTLY the opKeys the bindings resolve to. Send this exact map back as POST .../auth-preset's own editVersions.

bindings.description: The subset of the proposal the operator approved. Sending an empty array applies nothing.

editVersions.description: A3's compare-and-swap expectation, keyed by opKey — the exact map GET .../auth-preset's own editVersions returned. REQUIRED to name every opKey the submitted bindings resolve to (a missing key is rejected by name with 400), but NOT required at the schema level: when bindings is empty the handler short-circuits before ever checking this field, writes nothing and cannot conflict with anything, so an empty-bindings call may omit it entirely.

A3's fresh per-row edit_version of every op_overrides row this call touched, keyed by opKey — the only way a caller can write the SAME operation again without re-reading first, since this response carries no rows of its own. {} (never omitted) when applied is 0.

DirectiveTarget.description: Which operations a directive addresses: the string "*" for all of them, or one {method, path}.

Directive.description: One live-state directive. The wire shape is shared byte-for-byte with the mock plane's own POST {prefix}/state.

action.description: status: answer `status` until cleared. fail: answer `status` for the next N requests. delay: hold the response `ms` milliseconds, then serve it normally. pause: hold the response until the directive is cleared, or until the server's pause cap elapses — whichever comes first.

status.description: Required for status and fail (100..599). Must be absent for delay and pause — a non-zero status on either is rejected.

ms.description: delay only: how many milliseconds to hold the response before serving it normally. Required for delay (1..30000). Must be absent for every other action — a non-zero ms elsewhere is rejected.

once.description: fail only: fire exactly once. Implies n = 1.

n.description: fail only: how many requests are still to fail.

scenario.description: Reserved for P2. Sending it answers 501 rather than a misleading 400.

kind.description: Mirrors web/src/connect/probe.ts's ProbeResult kinds one-to-one, so the admin UI can compare this against the browser's own runProbe() result without a second vocabulary.

status.description: The HTTP status the target answered with. Present only for "http-error" — a redirect counts as an error here, since the server refuses to follow one (see internal/probe's own doc comment for why).

workspace.description: The slug the target's health route reported. Present for "ok" and "wrong-workspace".

message.description: Present only for "http-error": the target's own error message when it sent one, else the plain HTTP status text.

TrafficRow.description: One recorded request/response pair. Bodies are captured subject to redaction and a size cap — see `truncated`.

path.description: Normalised segments rejoined FOR DISPLAY ONLY: an encoded slash inside one segment is indistinguishable here from a real boundary. Never re-split it to reconstruct routing.

matchedKind.description: operation | endpoint | none — what answered this request.

truncated.description: The captured bodies are not what actually went over the wire. Both conversions below refuse such a row.

dropped.description: Rows the recorder had to drop under load. Non-zero means the list is incomplete and the UI must say so.

lastId.description: Pass back as `since` on the next poll.

EndpointView.description: A custom endpoint: a route this workspace serves that no spec declares.

editVersion.description: A3's per-row compare-and-swap token for this custom_endpoints row: this one schema is GET's list entry, POST's created-row response AND PUT's write response, so this field covers all three reads/writes at once.

kind.description: P6b: "http" for every row that predates streams, "sse" for a stream. "ws" (P6d) is a WebSocket endpoint: the same stream document plus reactive rules and echo; GET only, no responses.

reqSchema.description: P7a: the request body schema, exported as requestBody. Validated on write (shape, size, $refs); still never enforced on a request — that is P2.

body.description: Arbitrary JSON: the literal body this endpoint serves. Omitted means an empty pinned body — accepted, and almost never what anyone wants.

bodyRef.description: A6 (DESIGN §32.3): "asset:<name>" — the endpoint's pinned response IS this workspace's uploaded asset, served verbatim under its stored media type. Exclusive with body and mediaType (400 beside either). The PUT editor carries it inside responses[status].bodyRef instead.

kind.description: P6b: omitted means "http" (the row exactly as before). "sse" requires method GET, no status/body/mediaType (create) or an empty responses map with activeStatus 200 (update), and a stream document; refused by name otherwise. "ws" is refused until P6d. "ws" (P6d) is a WebSocket endpoint: the same stream document plus reactive rules and echo; GET only, no responses.

reqSchema.description: P7a: the request body schema, exported as requestBody. Validated on write (shape, size, $refs); still never enforced on a request — that is P2.

schema.description: P7a: the created response variant's inline schema. With no body beside it the response is GENERATED from this schema.

function.description: Lua that PRODUCES this endpoint's response instead of one being assembled for it (A18). It has a field of its own here, as bodyRef does, because this request builds ONE variant from flat fields where the PUT editor takes the variant whole through responses[]. Exclusive with body, bodyRef, mediaType, recipes and schemaPatch; refused by name on kind "sse"/"ws" (a stream's Lua goes in stream.tick.lua or stream.onFrame); compiled at write time, so unparseable source is a 400 carrying the parser's own words.

UpdateEndpointRequest.description: PUT's body: a full replacement of the endpoint's definition, the same shape GET/POST's EndpointView publishes minus the server-owned fields (id, canonicalPath, createdAt, updatedAt). Every field below besides method/path/editVersion is optional on the wire, but 'optional' does not mean 'preserved' here: an omitted field is replaced with its stated default, exactly as an omitted overrideOn/routeOff is, so a caller that only means to change method/path must still resend activeStatus and responses to keep them. Deliberately NOT CreateEndpointRequest's narrower shape — that would drop the ability to describe more than one response variant.

overrideOn.description: Omitted means true — the same default a brand-new endpoint gets.

activeStatus.description: Omitted defaults to 200 (the same default POST applies to an unset status). Since PUT is a full replacement, an omitted activeStatus overwrites whatever status was previously active.

responses.description: Omitted (or explicitly {}) defaults to an empty map, REMOVING every response the endpoint previously had — this is a full replacement, not a merge. Resend the endpoint's existing responses (from GET's own endpointView) to keep them while changing another field.

editVersion.description: A3's REQUIRED compare-and-swap expectation: the custom_endpoints row's edit_version as of the caller's last read (EndpointView.editVersion). An omitted field is rejected with 400, never treated as "no expectation" — that state exists only at customep.Repo's own unguarded Update verb, never on this wire. Unlike the operation PUT, 0 is REFUSED here rather than meaningful: a custom_endpoints row addressed by {eid} always already exists.

kind.description: P6b: omitted means "http" (the row exactly as before). "sse" requires method GET, no status/body/mediaType (create) or an empty responses map with activeStatus 200 (update), and a stream document; refused by name otherwise. "ws" is refused until P6d. "ws" (P6d) is a WebSocket endpoint: the same stream document plus reactive rules and echo; GET only, no responses.

reqSchema.description: P7a: the request body schema, exported as requestBody. Validated on write (shape, size, $refs); still never enforced on a request — that is P2.

CheckpointSummaryView.description: One checkpoint row — never the snapshot itself (§C): a list endpoint that answered every checkpoint's full config_snap would be a page-load cost that grows with the workspace's history, the same call P2b already made for scenarios. Also what POST .../checkpoints answers on 201.

kind.description: "manual" (the operator's own button) or "pre-destructive" (written by rollback and reset, in the same transaction as the destruction it protects). "auto" is also a legal value on the column but nothing in this slice writes it — the debounced trigger DESIGN §12:770-772 names is P2d.

label.description: User-visible text: the operator's own for a manual checkpoint (trimmed, non-empty, at most 200 runes), server-generated Russian for a pre-destructive one.

createdBy.description: The session user who caused this checkpoint. Nullable because the column allows it, but every row this build writes carries one.

hasData.description: Whether this checkpoint's data_snap IS NOT NULL (P3d) — derived at write time, never by decompressing the blob to answer this field. A restoreData:true rollback to a row with hasData:false is refused with 409 no_data_snapshot.

CreateCheckpointRequest.description: Snapshots the workspace's CURRENT settings, op_overrides rows, custom_endpoints rows and confirmed-resource configuration (resources, resource_decisions — P3b) into a new manual checkpoint. Does NOT bump the workspace's revision (nothing served changes when a history entry is written).

label.description: Trimmed, required non-empty, at most 200 runes (counted by rune, not byte — the UI is Russian). A longer or empty label is refused with 400 naming the field.

RollbackRequest.description: DESIGN §14:871 draws restoreData; confirmSlug is P3d's own addition, required exactly when restoreData is true. restoreData:true restores the checkpoint's entity rows (data_snap) alongside the workspace layer — see POST .../rollback/{cid}'s own description for the refusals this can hit.

restoreData.description: false or absent (default): the workspace layer (settings, overrides, custom endpoints) is restored; entity rows are read for this rollback's own pre-destructive checkpoint but never mutated. true (P3d): entity rows are restored too, from the target checkpoint's data_snap — requires confirmSlug and can be refused (409/413/500, see the route's own responses).

confirmSlug.description: Required, and must equal the workspace's own slug (read inside the same transaction as the write), exactly when restoreData is true — the same check POST .../resource-decisions and POST .../reset-data already require for a destructive call. Ignored when restoreData is false or absent.

RollbackResponseView.description: The workspace layer was restored to the target checkpoint's state and a new revision was allocated (max+1; revision numbers are never reused).

revision.description: The workspace's revision AFTER this call.

scenarioActive.description: Whether a scenario is (still) active for this workspace after the rollback. Rollback is allowed while a scenario is active and never deactivates it — the screen should warn that any key the active scenario names still overrides what was just restored.

dataRestored.description: P3d's no-op signal for the entity-data half of the restore: true when the restore ran for at least one family the checkpoint carried, false when every carried family was skipped (its resources row no longer exists) or the checkpoint carried none, and always false when restoreData was false or absent. Not an echo of the request's own restoreData — a RESOLVED family whose stored and live relations are both empty still counts as restored.

ResetOverridesResponseView.description: Screen 10's «сбросить всё к спеке»: every op_overrides row and every custom_endpoints row is deleted (settings survive — they are the workspace's identity, not edits to the spec), after a pre-destructive checkpoint is written.

revision.description: The workspace's revision AFTER this call. Unchanged from before the call when changed is false.

scenarioActive.description: Whether a scenario is (still) active for this workspace after the reset. Reset is allowed while a scenario is active and never deactivates it.

changed.description: False when there was nothing to reset (no op_overrides rows and no custom_endpoints rows already) — a true no-op: no checkpoint written, no revision bump.

ResetMode.description: reseed repopulates every confirmed family from the workspace's CURRENT configuration; clear deletes every entity row and mints nothing back. No third value exists.

ResetDataRequest.description: Both fields are required. An absent, empty or unrecognized mode answers 400 naming both legal values. confirmSlug is the workspace's own slug, re-checked inside the same transaction as the delete: entity data is the only state in this tree an anonymous caller can create and this route is IRREVERSIBLE, so the same confirmation the destructive MCP tools require is required here too.

confirmSlug.description: The workspace's own slug, required for both modes. An absent or empty value answers 409 confirm_slug_required and a present-but-wrong one 409 confirm_slug_mismatch; either way nothing is deleted. The comparison that decides is re-read INSIDE the transaction, so a rename racing the call is caught by it and not by the fence.

ResetDataSkippedFamily.description: One confirmed family a reseed left standing rather than repopulating, and why. clear never produces one of these — it has no per-family skip cases.

routeFamily.description: Identifies the family by the same value GET .../resources reports it under.

reason.description: stranded — the workspace's currently bound spec no longer declares this family. over_caps — the regenerated population would exceed the per-entity or per-resource storage cap. population_failed — generating the family's population itself failed partway through. group_skipped — a nested family and its confirmed parent reseed as one group (P3e D8.2): this family did not itself fail, but a sibling in its parent/child group did, and the whole group is skipped together rather than leaving a parent repopulated against children still scoped to its old keys, or the reverse.

ResetDataResult.description: changed is true when rows were deleted or inserted, false otherwise — a call over an empty roster, or a reseed in which every confirmed family was skipped, answers changed:false even though it ran to completion. deleted is the row count the delete actually removed, never an attempt. Success is always 200: a per-family failure is a skipped entry, never a refusal of the whole call.

deleted.description: The number of entity rows this call actually deleted.

skipped.description: One entry per confirmed family a reseed left standing. Always empty for clear.

PreviewRequest.description: The draft override PUT .../operations/{opKey} would save, plus the synthetic request preview renders it against.

opKey.description: Percent-encoded, exactly as MergedOperationView.opKey and the {opKey} path segment above.

status.description: A 3-digit status key naming which response variant to render directly (statusSource becomes "requested"). Omitted: the full precedence runs (when[], then active_status, then the document default) and statusSource reports which one supplied the answer.

query.description: A raw query string, evaluated against any query-gated when[] condition.

headers.description: Evaluated against any header-gated when[] condition.

body.description: A JSON request body, evaluated against any body-gated when[] condition. Arbitrary JSON.

pathParams.description: One entry per {param} segment of the workspace's basePath plus the operation's own path. Every declared parameter is REQUIRED here — a missing or empty one answers 400 missing_path_param, naming it.

PreviewRefusedView.description: Present when the resolved variant would serve no body at all for a reason other than 204/205/Degraded.

PreviewResultView.description: What the mock plane would answer with for the previewed request, once the draft is saved.

status.description: The HTTP status the precedence chose. Present even when routeOff is true — the status the plane would have used had the route been enabled.

body.description: Absent when noBody, routeOff or refused is set — those three are mutually exclusive. utf8 text or base64, per encoding.

noBody.description: 204/205, a Degraded variant, or an operation with no declared response variant at all.

routeOff.description: The composed row disables the route.

recipesBound.description: Set.Len() of the recipe bindings actually handed to the generator — bindings, not applications.

delayMs.description: The delay this operation would pay, computed and reported, never slept.

shadowedBy.description: The name of the active scenario whose snapshot supplied the composed row this result was built from, null when no scenario supplied one.

notes.description: A6: the traffic-note tokens a real request would have recorded, comma-joined ("asset_missing" for a bodyRef whose asset a preview never reads); absent when none.

ResourceSuggestion.description: One derived route family before any decision has been made about it. Confidence is a written constant, not a computed score: derivation is a yes/no predicate over the spec (a family either qualifies or it does not), and the column is reserved for a scoring pass this slice does not add.

routeFamily.description: The collection route's canonical path, relative (e.g. "/users").

idField.description: The JSON property an entity's id value is stored under. This is not always the detail route's path-parameter name (a route can be .../{userId} while the item body carries "id") — derivation reconciles the two and reports the property name here.

confidence.description: Always 1.0 today — see the object description.

ResourceSuggestionsView.description: GET /api/specs/{id}/resource-suggestions' whole body. Derivation runs once per spec: the first call derives and writes a sentinel row, every later call performs no re-derivation and reads back the same set. The sentinel itself never appears here.

RederiveResultView.description: POST /api/specs/{id}/rederive's whole body (decisions.md §D4.2). added/removed are route_family values that entered/left the newest generation across this call, sentinel excluded, diffed against the PREVIOUS newest generation — never against what any workspace has confirmed or declined.

changed.description: Whether a new generation was written.

generation.description: The generation that is newest for the spec after the call. On changed:false this is the generation that already was newest — never absent, so a client reads one shape either way.

added.description: route_family values present in the new generation and absent from the previous one.

removed.description: route_family values present in the previous generation and absent from the new one.

ResourceFamilyView.description: One route family's decision state inside a workspace, the shape both GET /api/workspaces/{id}/resources and POST .../resource-decisions answer with. On a row whose decision is null (never decided) or "declined", every confirmed-only field — resourceId, idField, writeForm, entityCount, byBaseScope — is null: nothing about the family has been materialized. A confirmed row's idField is the property name copied from the suggestion at confirm time (see ResourceSuggestion.idField); writeForm and entityCount are facts of the stored resource itself and can change afterward through ordinary POST/DELETE traffic without a new decision.

routeFamily.description: The collection route's canonical path, relative. Identifies the family on the decision route.

decision.description: null: the workspace has never decided this family.

resourceId.description: The resources table row id. Non-null only when decision is "confirmed".

idField.description: The JSON property populated entities are keyed by (see ResourceSuggestion.idField). Non-null only when decision is "confirmed".

writeForm.description: "bare": the collection route's declared POST body is structurally the same as the item schema, so POST on this family is taken over by storage. null: either the collection declares no eligible POST body or its schema differs from the item's, and POST keeps answering from the generator exactly as it did before confirmation — this is a real outcome of a confirmed resource, not only the unconfirmed default, so a null writeForm does not by itself mean the family is undecided.

entityCount.description: Rows currently stored for this resource, across EVERY scope for a nested family — not one parent row's slice of it. Non-null only when decision is "confirmed".

byBaseScope.description: entityCount broken down per declared base-path value (P3h, settings.basePathValues), in DECLARED order — an ARRAY, not an object keyed by the encoded tuple, so the order is the workspace's own rather than an encoding folded into a JSON key. One element per value the workspace currently declares, 0 for a value that holds no row yet. null (never an empty array), mirroring entityCount, exactly when decision is not "confirmed". For a workspace whose basePath carries no parameter this is a single element whose baseScope is "" — unchanged from every workspace before this field existed.

ResourceBaseScopeCount.description: One element of ResourceFamilyView.byBaseScope (P3h): a declared base value and the row count stored under it.

baseScope.description: The declared base value, encoded the same way every other scope tuple in this API is (internal/resources.EncodeScope) — "" for the implicit singleton a parameter-free basePath always serves.

entityCount.description: Rows currently stored for this resource under this one base value.

ResourceFamiliesView.description: GET /api/workspaces/{id}/resources' whole body: one row per suggestion of the workspace's bound spec, plus one row per confirmed resource whose family the current spec no longer suggests (an orphan left behind by re-binding to a different spec) — ordered by routeFamily among the rest. A workspace with no bound spec at all still reports its confirmed orphans, if any.

ResourceDecisionRequest.description: confirmSlug is optional on the wire and required by the server exactly when a resources row already exists for routeFamily: declining a family that was never confirmed needs none (there is nothing to destroy), while declining — or attempting to confirm — one that already has a resources row does, because that transition deletes the resource and every entity it holds. "Required conditionally on server-side state" has no JSON Schema expression that does not also force the field on the harmless case, so it stays optional here and the rule is enforced, and explained on refusal, by the response: a missing or wrong slug against an existing resource answers 409 confirm_slug_required or 409 confirm_slug_mismatch and writes nothing.

routeFamily.description: Identifies the family by the same value GET .../resource-suggestions and GET .../resources report as routeFamily.

confirmSlug.description: The workspace's own slug, checked against the workspace row inside the same transaction as the decline's delete — not against the route family or anything else. See the object description for exactly when it is required.

ResourceDecisionView.description: POST /api/workspaces/{id}/resource-decisions' 200 body: the one row the call just changed, in exactly the shape a ResourceFamiliesView row has — under the singular key "family" so the screen cannot mistake a single-row response for a list and skip updating from it.

DriftReportView.description: GET /api/workspaces/{id}/drift's whole body (mocker-p4a-triage decisions.md D4.2): the three things that silently stop working when a workspace is re-bound to a new spec version or a rederive drops a family, measured against the workspace's CURRENTLY bound spec and nothing else. Every array is [] rather than omitted or null when empty. hasDrift is the disjunction of the three arrays' emptiness — it can never disagree with them, because it is computed from nothing else. No row of any array carries a remedy: every repair this report names already has its own verb — DELETE /api/workspaces/{id}/operations/{opKey}, DELETE /api/workspaces/{id}/endpoints/{eid}, POST /api/workspaces/{id}/resource-decisions with state "declined". A workspace with no spec bound answers 200 with hasDrift false and three empty arrays: there is no spec to diverge from.

DriftOrphanedOverride.description: An op_overrides row whose (method, path) no operation of the bound spec produces — compared literally, never through the canonical form, the same key lookupOverride keys the serve path on.

path.description: Relative, the row's own stored key — not necessarily anything the bound spec still declares.

opKey.description: The percent-encoded segment DELETE /api/workspaces/{id}/operations/{opKey} accepts verbatim.

DriftOrphanedResource.description: A confirmed resources row whose routeFamily no suggestion of the bound spec's newest generation names.

entityCount.description: Across every scope of the family — what POST .../resource-decisions with state "declined" would destroy.

DriftShadowedEndpoint.description: A custom_endpoints row whose (method, canonicalPath) a spec operation of the bound spec also declares. precededSpec is custom_endpoints.created_at < specs.created_at for the bound spec, strictly — a hint carried beside the row, never a filter: every canonical collision is reported either way.

precededSpec.description: true when the endpoint was created before the bound spec was imported, so it cannot have been aimed at an operation that spec declares. false includes the equal-timestamp case.

ResourceEntityView.description: One row of GET /api/workspaces/{id}/resources/{family}/entities (decisions.md mocker-a4-mcp-reach D4): an entities row, re-tagged for the wire. data is the stored JSON object, already carrying the forced id — embedded raw, never re-decoded.

id.description: entities.id, an INTEGER PRIMARY KEY — the value the after cursor compares against, and what lastId echoes.

entityKey.description: The decimal string form of the entity's allocated seq — never the cursor value (unpadded decimal TEXT compares wrong under SQLite's BINARY collation).

scopeKey.description: The row's own encoded outer path-parameter values ("" for a family with no outer parameter).

baseScopeKey.description: The row's own encoded basePath-parameter value tuple ("" for a workspace whose basePath carries no parameter).

ResourceEntitiesView.description: GET /api/workspaces/{id}/resources/{family}/entities' whole body (decisions.md mocker-a4-mcp-reach D4): rows ordered by id ASC, plus lastId — the same cursor field name and mechanic TrafficPollView gives, because both key on a row id.

lastId.description: The highest id in rows, or the after cursor unchanged when rows is empty. Pass back as `after` on the next call.

StreamStatsView.description: GET /api/stream/stats's wire shape — stream.Stats (internal/stream/registry.go), marshalled as-is. Every counter is process-wide.

open.description: Live stream connections right now, across every workspace.

cap.description: The process-wide connection cap (64). A handshake over it answers 503.

refusedCap.description: Handshakes refused with 503 because the cap was reached, since the process started.

refusedUnsupported.description: Handshakes refused with 501 streaming_unsupported, since the process started.

coalescedNudges.description: Wake-ups dropped because the connection's one-slot signal was already full. No row is lost by a coalesced nudge; the count exists so coalescing can be seen rather than inferred.

byWorkspace.description: One row per workspace with at least one live connection, ascending by workspaceId. Empty when nothing is connected.

delayMs.description: Milliseconds to wait BEFORE this frame, 0..30000.

event.description: The SSE `event:` name; omitted means the browser's default message event. At most 64 bytes, no line break.

data.description: Any JSON value, written compact on one `data:` line. At most MOCKER_MAX_RESPONSE bytes.

loop.description: Restart from the first frame once the last is out (default false).

intervalMs.description: Milliseconds between generated frames; at least 100 (refused by name below that, never clamped).

schema.description: An inline JSON Schema object; every tick's body is generated from it with the workspace's own seed, deterministic per (seed, endpoint id, tick ordinal). No $ref — there is no document to resolve one against. Required unless `lua` is set, and refused together with it.

lua.description: Lua that produces each frame's body (A18 D10.1), exclusive with `schema` by name: exactly one of the two is required and a document carrying both is 400 tick_lua_and_schema. The source is the function body over one argument `ordinal` — the same number a generated body is seeded by — and returns the data: a table is JSON-encoded by the server, a string is the raw bytes of the `data:` line, and nil skips that firing with the connection left open. A body carrying a CR or LF, or one over MOCKER_MAX_RESPONSE, is a SKIPPED firing counted in the row's frames_skipped note. Unlike a generated tick, a Lua tick is NOT byte-identical at the same ordinal across connections.

StreamDefinition.description: P6b (DESIGN §30.2, §30.3): the stream document of a custom endpoint whose kind is "sse". At least one of timeline/tick. Validated by the one customep validator both writers and the preview route share.

closeWhenDone.description: Default true: close the connection once the timeline has drained (and does not loop) and there is no tick; false keeps it open, pinging, until MOCKER_STREAM_MAX_LIFETIME or the client leaves.

reactive.description: kind "ws" only (refused by name on "sse"). At most 100 rules; first match wins.

echo.description: kind "ws" only. An inbound frame no rule matched comes back as-is (same opcode); echo is the fallback, never a parallel producer.

onFrame.description: Lua run for every inbound frame while the connection is live (A18 D10.2), kind "ws" only (400 on_frame_on_sse). Present, it REPLACES reactive and echo entirely — both must be absent (400 on_frame_and_reactive, 400 on_frame_and_echo). The source is the function body over one argument `frame`: a TEXT frame that parses as a JSON object arrives as a table, anything else as the raw string. Verb-first return: nil for no reply, ("reply", data) for one text frame, ("close", code, reason?) for the closing handshake with code 1000 or 4000..4999. A reply enters the same per-connection send budget a reactive reply does; a Lua error or a malformed return drops that reply, counts it in the row's on_frame_errors note, and leaves the hook called for later frames.

notRun.description: True when the frame's PLACE on the time axis is real but its body was never produced: a `tick.lua` preview shares one 10-second budget across every frame it lays out, and past it the rest are labelled rather than dropped, since a shorter list would read as "the stream ends here". `data` is null on such a frame.

frames.description: The first at most 50 frames on one time axis, as a client would receive them; tick bodies generated with endpoint id 0.

truncated.description: The stream would send more than the preview shows (a looping timeline or a tick always does).

maxBytesPerSec.description: An ESTIMATE of the connection's peak outbound rate: the larger of the timeline's bytes over its own duration (at least one second) and the tick's first body over its interval — what §30.12's amplifier amounts to for this definition.

rules.description: P6d: the draft's reactive rule count — inbound behaviours have no time axis, so they are reported, not laid out.

echo.description: P6d: whether the draft echoes unmatched frames.

nominalRate.description: True when `maxBytesPerSec` is a SAMPLE of what actually ran rather than a bound — always the case with a `tick.lua` producer, whose next firing may return anything. An unlabelled nominal number reads as a guarantee it is not.

method.description: Must be GET for kind sse.

kind.description: Only a stream draft has frames to preview. "ws" (P6d) answers rules/echo beside the frames; the contract said "sse" alone until P6e, a drift from the handler, which accepted both.

StreamMockStatsView.description: P6b (D10): the MOCK plane's own stream registry — a separate instance from the admin feed's, capped PER WORKSPACE by MOCKER_STREAM_MAX_CONNS. open/byWorkspace count live SSE mock connections; refusedUnsupported and coalescedNudges are carried for shape and stay 0 on this plane.

cap.description: The per-WORKSPACE cap (MOCKER_STREAM_MAX_CONNS); 0 refuses every stream handshake.

id.description: Registry-minted connection id (P6c D2): a counter from 1 per process, never reused while it runs.

endpointId.description: The custom endpoint (kind sse) this connection is on.

kind.description: "sse" — the only stream kind until P6d.

remoteAddr.description: The peer as the traffic row records it (peerIp).

frames.description: Frames written so far, pushed ones included.

pushed.description: Frames an operator pushed through POST .../frames.

skipped.description: Generated tick bodies over MOCKER_MAX_RESPONSE, skipped and counted.

framesIn.description: P6d: inbound frames read on a WebSocket connection; 0 on an SSE connection.

open.description: The workspace's live connection count (unfiltered — what the per-workspace cap is compared against).

cap.description: MOCKER_STREAM_MAX_CONNS, per workspace; the same number GET /api/stream/stats reports under mock.cap.

event.description: The SSE `event:` name; omitted means the browser's default message event. At most 64 bytes, no line break — the same rule a timeline frame's event passes.

data.description: Any JSON value, written compact on one `data:` line. At most MOCKER_MAX_RESPONSE bytes — the same rule a timeline frame's data passes, refused with the same words.

frameId.description: The `id:` the frame went out under — the connection's next ordinal, interleaved with its timeline and tick frames.

code.description: Close status code: 1000 or 4000..4999 (the application range; 1xxx and 3xxx are refused by name).

reason.description: At most 123 bytes (a close frame payload minus the code).

StreamRule.description: P6d (decisions.md mocker-p6d-websocket D2–D4): one reactive rule of a kind "ws" endpoint. An inbound TEXT frame whose payload is a JSON object is matched against the rules in order (when[] is the same Condition language op_overrides use: in=body reads the frame's top-level keys, in=query/header read the HANDSHAKE's, captured once); the first match answers. At least one of data/close.

data.description: Any JSON value, sent as ONE text frame, at most MOCKER_MAX_RESPONSE bytes.

AssetView.description: One uploaded asset. url is the mock-plane address it is served at, built from the request's own scheme and port exactly as a workspace's url is, so it is what an asset_url recipe writes and what a frontend fetches.

sha256.description: lower-case hex of the stored bytes; the mock route's strong ETag

confirmSlug.description: The workspace's own slug, exactly; checked inside the delete's transaction.

WorkspaceExportDocument.description: The mockerBundle v6 document (DESIGN §17) with two optional additions: `data` (a mockerData document of entity rows, present only with includeData=true on a workspace that confirmed a family) and `spec.inline` (the spec's bytes as uploaded, as one JSON string, present only with includeSpec=true). `entities` stays null (P3d: rows live in `data`). Keys are sorted, so the document diffs cleanly in git.

spec.description: `{hash, name, inline}`; `inline` is null unless includeSpec=true.

data.description: `{mockerData, families: [{routeFamily, rows: [...]}]}` — the checkpoint data_snap document.

name.description: The new workspace's name; defaults to the document's workspace.name.

slug.description: Optional; uniquified from the name when omitted.

specId.description: Bind to this already-imported spec regardless of what the document names.
The spec the workspace was bound to; null when the document named none.

specCreated.description: True when the spec was imported by this call from the document's spec.inline.

entitiesRestored.description: How many confirmed families received rows from the document's `data`.

ForkWorkspaceRequest.description: POST /api/workspaces/{id}/fork's body (P4b); every field optional, an empty body is legal.

name.description: The copy's name; defaults to the source's name plus « (копия)».

slug.description: Optional; uniquified from the name when omitted.

includeData.description: Copy the entity rows of every confirmed family.

SessionClearRequest.description: DELETE .../session's optional body (A13): the target whose directives to remove, and optionally which action.

action.description: Remove only this action on the target; omitted removes every action on it.

schema.description: An inline JSON Schema; the same rules a response schema has.

EndpointParameter.description: One declared parameter of a custom endpoint. A `path` parameter must name a {name} segment of the row's own path; an undeclared {name} segment is derived at export time as a required string.

operationId.description: Unique across the workspace's custom rows AND the bound spec's own operationIds; 409 operation_id_taken otherwise.

EndpointOperation.description: P7a (DESIGN §34.3): the OpenAPI operation fields a custom endpoint carries for the export. Absent on a row that declares none.

EndpointRefConflict.description: One row of an endpoint_ref_unresolved 409's details (P7a, D6): a custom endpoint whose schema, reqSchema or parameter schema carries a `$ref` the spec the verb would bind cannot resolve.

endpointId.description: The stored row's id on a rebind (PATCH); omitted on an import and on a rollback, whose rows are only in the document yet.

reason.description: Where the reference sits and the pointer that does not resolve, in the validator's own words.

post.summary: Open a session
post.description: The only state-changing route exempt from the X-CSRF-Token check — it has no session to take a token from yet. The Content-Type and Origin checks still apply.

200.description: Session opened. The cookie is set on this response.

401.description: Invalid credentials. Deliberately the SAME answer for a wrong password and an unknown name — the UI must not distinguish them either.

429.description: Rate limited: 10 attempts per minute, bucketed by (client address, submitted name).

post.summary: Close the current session

204.description: Session cleared. Idempotent: no session is still a 204.

get.description: The UI's session probe on every load. A 401 here is the normal anonymous answer, not an error to report.

parameters.name: all
parameters.description: Pass "1" to list every workspace rather than only the caller's own.

200.description: A bare JSON array, not an envelope.

post.summary: Create a workspace

409.description: edit_conflict: editVersion no longer matches the workspace's stored edit_version — another write landed between this caller's read and this write. `details` is either the workspace's current document (WorkspaceConflictDetails) or, when the workspace was deleted meanwhile, the gone tombstone {"gone": true, "editVersion": null}. Or endpoint_ref_unresolved (P7a, D6): specId names a spec into which a stored custom endpoint's schema, reqSchema or parameter schema `$ref` does not resolve; details is a list of EndpointRefConflict rows and nothing is written — edit or delete those rows first.

post.summary: Import a document
post.description: 200 with duplicate: true when the same bytes are already stored; 201 otherwise. A document that parses with warnings still imports — the report says what was degraded.

200.description: Already imported; the existing spec is returned.

get.summary: Operations as this workspace will serve them
get.description: An empty array when the workspace has no spec attached — not a 404.

get.summary: The override document for one operation

409.description: edit_conflict: editVersion no longer matches the row's stored edit_version — another write landed between this caller's read and this write. `details` is either the operation's current document (OverrideConflictDetails) or, when the row was deleted meanwhile, the gone tombstone {"gone": true, "editVersion": null}.

delete.summary: Drop the override, back to what the spec says
delete.description: 204 when there was nothing to delete (the workspace revision did not move); 200 with the new revision when a document was actually removed.

get.description: Writes nothing. The operator must see the identity/token mapping before anything is applied, which is why preview and apply are two routes rather than one.

post.summary: Apply the approved bindings

409.description: edit_conflict: one or more op_overrides rows the submitted bindings resolve to no longer match the editVersions the caller sent — another write landed between this caller's read of GET .../auth-preset and this write. `details.staleVersions` is a map keyed by opKey, holding only the rows that disagreed, with a null value meaning that row is gone.

post.summary: Render what a draft override would produce once saved
post.description: Writes nothing, bumps no revision and takes no checkpoint. Runs PUT's own three validation gates on the draft before rendering it through the same assembly the mock plane serves real traffic with.

400.description: invalid_draft (the draft fails the same three checks PUT runs), no_spec (the workspace has no spec attached) or missing_path_param (a path parameter the located route declares is missing or empty) — the wire code names which.

404.description: operation_not_found: opKey names no operation in the attached spec.

409.description: custom_endpoint_wins: an enabled custom endpoint occupies this (method, path) and would outrank the spec operation, or opKey names a custom endpoint directly.

post.summary: Force a status, or fail N times
post.description: Answers with the full directive list, so the caller never has to re-read to learn the new state.

400.description: Malformed directive — including one over the directive-sized body cap (reported here as 400, not 413), and a directive that carries a "scenario" key (A17): this route's shared decoder still recognizes that field, but scenario switching has its own dedicated route now (POST .../scenarios/{id}/activate, .../scenarios/deactivate) and is refused here rather than acted on.

delete.summary: Clear every directive, or one target's (A13)
delete.description: Without a body: removes EVERY directive in force for the workspace (the pre-A13 shape). With a body naming `target` (`"*"` or `{method, path}`) and optionally `action`: removes only that target's directives — every action on it, or the one named — and releases a request parked by a pause on it. A body that names no target is refused 400, never read as "everything". The same optional body works on the mock plane's `DELETE {prefix}/state`.

get.description: Oldest first. Each entry is a name, a date and whether it is the active one — never the snapshot itself; fetch GET .../scenarios/{sid} for that.

post.summary: Save the workspace's current state as a new scenario

409.description: A scenario with this name already exists, a scenario is already active for this workspace and from was not given (deactivate it first, or pass from to clone instead — A10), or the workspace kept changing while it was being snapshotted and from was not given (retry — A11; a clone never reads the workspace's own layer, so this cause cannot fire when from is present).

post.summary: Deactivate the workspace's scenario, if any
post.description: Takes no request body. This slice's own addition, not one of DESIGN §14's named verbs: PATCH .../workspaces/{id} cannot express "no scenario" — its scenarioId field is a bare int64-or-null that collapses null and absent — so deactivation gets its own route. A no-op when the workspace already has no active scenario (A7): the same revision comes back, no write at all.

get.description: What screen 5's active-scenario banner reads to learn which settings/overrides keys a running scenario currently masks.

404.description: No such scenario id in this workspace — including one that belongs to a DIFFERENT workspace (A8): the two answer identically, so this workspace never learns which is which.

put.description: Changes the scenario's name and nothing else — the stored snapshot, its created_at and whether it is the workspace's active scenario are untouched, and no revision is bumped (a rename does not change what any runtime serves). Renaming a scenario a running test suite names on the mock plane's own scenario-switch route is a breaking change for that suite.

404.description: No such scenario id in this workspace (A8).

409.description: Two distinct meanings share this status on this route, told apart by error.code: conflict — a scenario with this name already exists in this workspace; or edit_conflict (A3) — editVersion no longer matches the row's stored edit_version, another write landed between this caller's read and this write, and details is either the scenario's current document (ScenarioConflictDetails) or, when the scenario was deleted meanwhile, the gone tombstone {"gone": true, "editVersion": null}. This response object is deliberately separate from the inline Error-typed 409 this route answered before A3.

delete.description: Deleting the ACTIVE scenario deactivates it in the same write (ON DELETE SET NULL) and bumps the workspace's revision, so the next request stops being served from a runtime built over a scenario that no longer exists (A9).

404.description: No such scenario id in this workspace (A8).

post.summary: Activate a scenario
post.description: Takes no request body — {sid} in the path is the entire instruction. Composed at request time over the workspace's own layer, never restored over it (DESIGN §4): writes exactly one column (scenario_id) plus a revision bump. Re-activating the already-active scenario is a no-op — same scenarioId and revision back, no write at all (A7).

404.description: No such scenario id in this workspace — including one that belongs to a DIFFERENT workspace (A8).

post.summary: Dial the workspace's own external health route, server-side
post.description: DESIGN §14 screen 4's SERVER half of the two-sided «Проверить»: mocker dials {workspace.url}{reservedPrefix}/health by the workspace's externally reachable name — assembled server-side from the workspace record plus a trust-proxy-gated scheme whitelisted to exactly "http" or "https" and a port taken from the request's Host only when it is a bare decimal number, never from this request's body, query, or an unvalidated header value — and reports the outcome. Compared against the browser's own probe (web/src/connect/probe.ts), a server-yes/browser-no split diagnoses a missing root CA in the caller's browser rather than an opaque network error.

200.description: The probe ran. This route itself always answers 200 once the workspace is found — the TARGET's own failure (refused connection, timeout, wrong body, non-2xx status) is reported inside the body via "kind", never as this route's own status.

get.summary: Rows recorded since a given id
get.description: The live-tail primitive. Pass the previous answer's lastId back as `since`.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Return rows with an id strictly greater than this.

get.summary: The traffic feed over Server-Sent Events
get.description: P6a (decisions.md mocker-p6a-sse; DESIGN §30.10). Holds the connection open and writes one SSE frame per batch of new rows: `id: <lastId>`, `event: traffic`, `data: <a TrafficPollView>` — the SAME JSON object GET .../traffic/poll answers with, at most 200 rows per frame, consecutive frames until the connection has caught up. A `:ping` comment line goes out every MOCKER_STREAM_PING seconds on an idle connection. The cursor is the `Last-Event-ID` header when present and a positive integer (the browser's own reconnect sends it), `?since=` otherwise, zero when neither. A connection lives at most 900 seconds and is closed when the session or the workspace fails its periodic recheck (MOCKER_STREAM_SESSION_RECHECK) — the client resumes on Last-Event-ID and misses no row. The poll route stays wired beside this one and is the fallback whenever this handshake is refused: 503 when the process-wide connection cap (64) is reached or the server is shutting down, 501 streaming_unsupported when the response writer cannot take a write deadline. The screen consumes this route through the browser's own EventSource, not through the generated client — a generated hook here would buffer a stream that never ends; web/src/api/coverage.test.ts recognises the EventSource call shape.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Start after this traffic row id, exactly as GET .../traffic/poll reads it. Ignored when Last-Event-ID is present and positive.

parameters.name: Last-Event-ID
parameters.description: Sent by EventSource on its own reconnect: the `id:` of the last frame it received. Wins over `since` when present and a positive integer.

200.description: An SSE stream that does not end on its own: `Content-Type: text/event-stream`, `Cache-Control: no-store`, `X-Accel-Buffering: no`. Each frame's `data:` line is one TrafficPollView.

501.description: The response writer this request arrived on cannot stream — no write deadline or flush (a proxy that unwraps into something that cannot flush, an in-process loopback). `code` is `streaming_unsupported`. Nothing was written before the refusal; poll instead.

503.description: Refused before the handshake: the process-wide stream connection cap is reached, the server is shutting down, or no stream registry is wired in this deployment. `code` is `service_unavailable`. Poll instead.

post.summary: Pin a recorded response onto the operation it matched
post.description: Takes no request body. Refuses with 409 when the row matched no spec operation, when the operation it matched is gone or belongs to another spec, or when the capture was truncated/redacted — pinning such a row would ship a body the client never actually received.

post.summary: Turn a recorded response into a custom endpoint
