post.description: Takes no request body. Same truncated/redacted refusal as to-override, for the same reason.

post.summary: Create a custom endpoint

409.description: Two distinct meanings share this status, told apart by error.code: conflict — an override or another custom endpoint already sits at the same (method, path); operation_id_taken (P7a, D3) — operation.operationId is already held by another custom endpoint of the workspace or by an operation of the bound spec (the message names the holder). Neither writes anything.

post.summary: The first frames a stream endpoint draft would send
post.description: P6b (decisions.md mocker-p6b-sse-mock D13). Read-only in effect, agent-only (no screen calls this route — see web/src/api/coverage.test.ts's EXEMPT entry; preview_endpoint is its MCP tool): takes a draft in the create-request shape, runs the SAME write-time validation POST .../endpoints runs (a refused draft is refused here with the same message), writes no row, bumps no revision, takes no auto checkpoint, and lays the first at most 50 frames out on one time axis — timeline frames as authored, tick frames generated from the inline schema with the workspace's own seed and endpoint id 0. Only kind "sse" previews.

put.description: Full replacement, not a partial merge: the caller resends every field it wants kept. A move onto a (method, path) another custom endpoint or an op_overrides row already occupies answers 409 rather than overwriting or silently stranding the other row.

409.description: Three distinct meanings share this status on this route, told apart by error.code: conflict — the shared meaning every other 409 on this plane carries (internal/httpx/respond.go#CodeConflict) — a move onto a (method, path) another custom endpoint or an op_overrides row already occupies; or edit_conflict (A3) — editVersion no longer matches the row's stored edit_version, another write landed between this caller's read and this write, and details is either the endpoint's current document (EndpointConflictDetails) or, when the row was deleted meanwhile, the gone tombstone {"gone": true, "editVersion": null}. This response object is deliberately separate from #/components/responses/Conflict, which six other routes still use unchanged for the first meaning alone. The third, operation_id_taken (P7a, D3), is the same refusal POST answers: operation.operationId is held by another custom endpoint or a spec operation.

get.description: Newest first. Each entry is an id, a kind, a label, a date and who created it — never the snapshot itself.

post.summary: Save the workspace's current state as a new manual checkpoint

409.description: The workspace kept changing while it was being snapshotted; retry.

delete.description: Removes one checkpoint row. Bumps no revision and takes no pre-destructive checkpoint of its own — this is not a restore. Any kind may be deleted, including the newest row and the last one still in the workspace's history: an empty checkpoint history is a legal state, it is what every workspace starts in.

404.description: No such checkpoint id in this workspace — including one that belongs to a DIFFERENT workspace: the two answer identically, so this workspace never learns which is which.

post.summary: Restore the workspace layer to a checkpoint
post.description: Settings, operation overrides and custom endpoints are all restored wholesale (never merged) to the checkpoint's snapshot. The snapshot's confirmed-family configuration (resources, resource_decisions — P3b) is restored UPSERT-ONLY: a row the snapshot names is written back, but no row is ever deleted by this call, so a family confirmed after the checkpoint survives a rollback to it. restoreData:true (P3d) additionally restores the entity rows themselves from the checkpoint's data_snap: a family declined after the checkpoint comes back both configured AND populated, requires confirmSlug (checked inside the same transaction as everything else this call writes), and is refused rather than run partially when the target checkpoint carries no entity data, its stored document is unreadable, or this rollback's own pre-destructive capture of the CURRENT entity state degrades past the size cap — see the 409/413 responses below. Protected by a pre-destructive checkpoint of the CURRENT state (settings AND, since P3d, entity rows) written in the same transaction, and a new revision is allocated (max+1). Allowed while a scenario is active — see scenarioActive on the response.

400.description: Malformed body — including a body naming restoreData or confirmSlug with the wrong JSON type.

404.description: No such workspace, or no such checkpoint id in this workspace — including one that belongs to a DIFFERENT workspace (the two answer identically).

409.description: Five distinct meanings share this status, told apart by error.code: conflict — the workspace kept changing while it was being snapshotted, retry; confirm_slug_required — restoreData:true and confirmSlug was omitted or empty; confirm_slug_mismatch — restoreData:true and confirmSlug did not match the workspace's own slug, checked inside the same transaction as everything else this call writes; no_data_snapshot — restoreData:true against a checkpoint whose data_snap IS NULL (it predates P3d, or its own capture degraded). Every one of the four writes nothing. endpoint_ref_unresolved (P7a, D6) — the checkpoint's endpoint rows carry a `$ref` the workspace's CURRENT spec cannot resolve (a rollback restores layers, never the spec binding); details is a list of EndpointRefConflict rows, endpointId omitted, and nothing is written.

413.description: Three distinct meanings share this status, told apart by error.code: too_large — the CONFIGURATION half of this rollback's own pre-destructive snapshot (settings, overrides, custom endpoints) exceeds the checkpoint size cap; data_snapshot_too_large (P3d) — restoreData:true and the ENTITY-DATA half of that same pre-destructive snapshot degrades past its own cap, so unchecking restoreData is what would let the rollback through; too_large (httpx) — the request body itself exceeded the plane-wide limit before this route ever saw it. Every one writes nothing.

500.description: Server-side failure. Most causes are generic (the message is deliberately vague; the detail is in the server log), but restoreData:true against a checkpoint whose data_snap decodes yet fails validation — a hand-built or otherwise corrupted document, never one this build itself writes — answers 500 rather than a 4xx, because nothing a client sent caused it.

post.summary: Reset the workspace layer to the spec
post.description: Screen 10's «сбросить всё к спеке»: deletes every op_overrides row and every custom_endpoints row (the auth preset and any custom endpoint go with it — neither is in the spec), after writing a pre-destructive checkpoint. settings are NOT touched. Takes no request body. A reset that would delete nothing is a no-op: 200, changed:false, no checkpoint written, no revision bump.

200.description: Reset (or a no-op — see changed on the response).

409.description: The workspace kept changing while it was being snapshotted; retry.

post.summary: Reseed or clear a workspace's stored entity rows
post.description: The RESET half of the resources surface, entirely separate from reset-overrides above: this route never touches op_overrides, custom_endpoints or settings, and reset-overrides never touches an entities row — the two verbs partition the workspace into configuration and data and each resets only its own half. mode:"reseed" deletes every confirmed family's entity rows and repopulates them from the workspace's CURRENT configuration (not the configuration a family was originally confirmed under), resetting each repopulated family's id counter to its population size. mode:"clear" deletes every entity row of every confirmed family and mints nothing back; the id counter is left exactly where the last write left it, so a client that already consumed and deleted an id will not see it minted again. Both modes are IRREVERSIBLE: a checkpoint's config_snap carries which families are confirmed and how they are configured, never the entity rows themselves, so there is nothing this route's own effect can be rolled back from. A reseed skips (rather than refuses on) a family the bound spec no longer declares (stranded), a family whose regenerated population would exceed a storage cap (over_caps), a family whose generation itself fails (population_failed), or a family sharing a nested parent/child group with one of the above, skipped as a group rather than left half-repopulated (group_skipped, P3e D8.2) — every other confirmed family is still repopulated, and every skip is named in the response so an operator can see which data did not come back and why. Writes no checkpoint of its own and does not bump the workspace's revision: the runtime cache is keyed on configuration alone, and this route changes none.

200.description: Reset (or a no-op — see changed on the response). Always 200: a per-family failure is reported as an entry of skipped, never as a refusal of the whole call.

400.description: bad_request: mode is absent, empty or names neither "reseed" nor "clear".

409.description: Three distinct meanings share this status, told apart by error.code, and every one of them writes nothing: confirm_slug_required — confirmSlug was omitted; confirm_slug_mismatch — confirmSlug did not match the workspace's own slug, checked inside the same transaction as the delete; stale_config — mode:"reseed" only: the workspace's identity (created_at), an input the generator read while building the population (spec_id, scenario_id, and, with no scenario active, settings.seed and the effective listSize), or the confirmed-family roster itself changed between preparation and the write.

get.summary: List a spec's derived resource-family suggestions
get.description: Derives once per spec and remembers it with a sentinel row (visible nowhere in this response), so this call is cheap to repeat from the screen: the first caller pays the derivation, every later one reads back the same set. A route family qualifies when its collection route (X) and detail route (X/{}) both exist and X itself carries no path parameter; the id property is read off the detail route's item schema.

post.summary: Re-run family derivation over an already-imported spec
post.description: Re-runs the same derivation Import and the lazy backfill use, over the spec's stored normalized document, and writes the result as a new resource_suggestions generation if and only if it differs from the current newest one. Spec-scoped, never workspace-scoped: derivation is a function of a spec's own document, so one call changes what every workspace bound to it sees. Touches no workspace table at all — not workspaces, resources, resource_decisions, entities, checkpoints, scenarios, op_overrides, custom_endpoints or traffic — bumps no workspace's revision, and takes no auto checkpoint. added/removed are computed over two GENERATIONS of resource_suggestions, sentinel excluded, never over what any workspace has confirmed or declined. A concurrent write to the same spec's newest generation between this call's pre-read and its own write answers 409 stale_generation and writes nothing.

200.description: The current newest generation after the call — Changed is false when the derived row set already matched it and nothing was written.

get.summary: List a workspace's resource families and their decision state
get.description: One row per suggestion of the workspace's bound spec, plus one row per confirmed resource the current spec no longer suggests (see ResourceFamiliesView). Reading this CAN derive: it calls the same lazy-backfill entry point GET /api/specs/{id}/resource-suggestions does, so whichever of the two routes is called first on a spec with no suggestions yet pays the derivation cost.

post.summary: Confirm or decline a route-family resource
post.description: The whole decision lifecycle for one family, in a single call: state="confirmed" materializes a resources row and populates it deterministically from the same generator that serves the detail route today; state="declined" writes the decision and, if a resources row already existed, deletes it and every entity it holds. Both transitions run as one transaction with the workspace's revision bump. Nothing about a confirmed resource is editable through this route or any other — there is no PUT and no re-populate; a resource that is wrong is declined and confirmed again.

404.description: unknown_family: routeFamily names neither a suggestion of the workspace's bound spec nor an existing resources row. The resources-row check runs first, so a workspace whose spec has since been re-bound (or that has none) can still decline a family it once confirmed — this code is reached only when there is truly nothing to act on.

409.description: Nine distinct meanings share this status, told apart by error.code, and every one of them writes nothing: already_confirmed — state="confirmed" and routeFamily already carries a confirmed resources row, including one the current spec no longer suggests; confirm_slug_required — state="declined" against an existing resources row and confirmSlug was omitted; confirm_slug_mismatch — the same case, but confirmSlug did not match the workspace's own slug; stale_config — the workspace's identity (created_at, slug) or an input the generator read while building the population (spec_id, scenario_id, settings.seed, the effective listSize) changed between generation and the write transaction; entity_limit — the confirm's generated population would exceed the per-resource row cap or byte-total cap; population_failed — a generated detail body failed to decode as a JSON object partway through population. parent_not_confirmed — state="confirmed" against a nested family (one whose route carries exactly one outer path parameter) whose parent family does not itself carry a confirmed resources row, read inside this same transaction (P3e D5.1). child_confirmed — state="declined" against a family that is the parent of a still-confirmed child family; the decline is refused rather than cascaded, and the message names the child families (P3e D7.1). base_scope_undeclared — state="confirmed" in a workspace whose settings.basePath carries a {param} while settings.basePathValues declares no value to populate it with, so the confirm has no base scope to write rows under; checked inside this same transaction, beside the parent check and for that check's own reason (P3h D6.4).

get.summary: The three silent-drift signals for one workspace, against its currently bound spec
get.description: Read-only, agent-only (no screen calls this route — see web/src/api/coverage.test.ts's EXEMPT entry): an orphaned operation override, an orphaned confirmed resource family, and a custom endpoint shadowing a spec operation. Measured against the workspace's currently bound spec and nothing else — there is no baseline column recording what it was configured against, so a re-bind to a different spec and a rederive minting a narrower generation over the same spec are not distinguished. Reading this CAN derive: it calls the same lazy-backfill entry point GET /api/specs/{id}/resource-suggestions does, so it may be the first route to pay the derivation cost on a spec that has never had its suggestions computed. A workspace with no spec bound answers 200 with hasDrift false and three empty arrays. Carries no remedy field: every repair already has its own verb — DELETE /api/workspaces/{id}/operations/{opKey}, DELETE /api/workspaces/{id}/endpoints/{eid}, POST /api/workspaces/{id}/resource-decisions with state "declined".

parameters.name: family
parameters.description: Already percent-encoded (url.PathEscape of the family's routeFamily). Go's ServeMux unescapes each path segment on its own, so the server reads it back decoded — pass it exactly as ResourceFamilyView.routeFamily reports it, url.PathEscape'd.

get.summary: A confirmed resource family's entity rows, paginated and scope-filtered
get.description: Read-only, agent-only (no screen calls this route — see web/src/api/coverage.test.ts's EXEMPT entry; decisions.md mocker-a4-mcp-reach D4). limit defaults to 100 and clamps silently to 500 — it never answers 400. after is an id cursor: pass the previous answer's lastId back to continue. scopeKey and baseScopeKey are both optional filters; omitted, either axis is unfiltered. 404 unknown_family whenever routeFamily does not resolve to a confirmed resources row of this workspace, for every reason (never suggested, declined, or the workspace has no spec bound) — one code for all three, the same taxonomy POST .../resource-decisions already answers with.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Return rows with an id strictly greater than this.

parameters.name: scopeKey
parameters.description: Filter to one nested family's own encoded scope; omitted, every scope is returned.

parameters.name: baseScopeKey
parameters.description: Filter to one declared basePath scope; omitted, every base scope is returned.

404.description: unknown_family: routeFamily does not resolve to a confirmed resources row of this workspace, for any reason.

parameters.name: family
parameters.description: url.PathEscape of the family's routeFamily, exactly as for the list route.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: The row's entityKey — for a family the mock plane populated, a decimal integer; 1..128 characters of [A-Za-z0-9._~-].

put.summary: Create or replace one entity row of a confirmed family by key
put.description: A11. The body's data becomes the row verbatim except data[idField], which is overwritten with the key coerced to the family's id type — the key IS the identity. A decimal key raises resources.seq to at least that value, so the mock plane's next POST cannot collide with it. Caps: the family's row and byte limits (409 entity_limit). No revision bump, no auto checkpoint; undo is a checkpoint restored with restoreData: true.

200.description: The stored row; created says whether it was inserted or replaced.

delete.summary: Delete one entity row of a confirmed family by key
delete.description: A11. The optional body names the scope (scopeKey, baseScopeKey; both default to "", the top-level scope). 404 entity_not_found when no row has that key in that scope; 404 unknown_family when the family is not confirmed. No confirmSlug: this removes one row, the same thing the mock plane's anonymous DELETE does.

get.summary: Process-wide health of the SSE traffic feed
get.description: Read-only, agent-only (no screen calls this route — see web/src/api/coverage.test.ts's EXEMPT entry; get_stream_stats is its MCP tool). Not workspace-scoped, because the connection cap is not: `open` counts live stream connections across every workspace, `cap` is the fixed process-wide ceiling, `refusedCap` and `refusedUnsupported` are the two refusal counters since the process started (kept apart because they are different failures with different repairs), `coalescedNudges` counts wake-ups dropped because a connection was already reading (no row is lost by that), and `byWorkspace` lists only workspaces holding at least one live connection. 503 service_unavailable when no stream registry is wired in this deployment.

get.summary: Live SSE connections of the workspace's mock endpoints
get.description: P6c (decisions.md mocker-p6c-live-conns D1, D8). Read-only, agent-only (no screen calls this route — see web/src/api/coverage.test.ts's EXEMPT entry; list_stream_connections is its MCP tool). Lists the MOCK plane's live connections of this workspace — one row per connection with its id, endpoint, peer, open time and three live counters — beside the per-workspace cap. The admin plane's own traffic-feed connections are not listed. Optional endpointId narrows the rows; open stays the workspace's whole count. 503 service_unavailable when no mock stream registry is wired.

delete.description: P6c (decisions.md mocker-p6c-live-conns D5). Agent-only (close_stream_connection is its MCP tool; see coverage.test.ts's EXEMPT entry). Cancels the connection: no final frame (SSE has no close frame), the socket closes, the connection's single traffic row is written with closed:admin in its notes. A browser EventSource reconnects on its own and appears as a NEW connection with a NEW id. No confirmSlug — a connection is not workspace data. Writes no row, bumps no revision, takes no auto checkpoint. 404 connection_not_found when the id is not a live connection of THIS workspace (never issued, already closed — including a second DELETE racing the first — or another workspace's).

post.summary: Push one frame into one live SSE connection
post.description: P6c (decisions.md mocker-p6c-live-conns D3, D4, D6). Agent-only (push_stream_frame is its MCP tool; see coverage.test.ts's EXEMPT entry). Validates the frame exactly as a timeline frame is validated at write time (same words), queues it into the connection's RAM inbox (16 frames deep) and WAITS until the connection's own loop has written it — the answer carries the `id:` it went out under. The frame lives in the connection alone: never stored, never replayed to a later connection, lost with the connection if unwritten. Writes no row, bumps no revision, takes no auto checkpoint. 404 connection_not_found (list again); 409 inbox_full (the frame was NOT queued); 409 connection_closed (the connection ended while the frame was queued — not written); 504 push_timeout (not written within 2 × MOCKER_STREAM_FRAME_TIMEOUT — the frame STAYS queued and may still be written).

504.description: push_timeout: the loop did not write the frame within two frame timeouts; it stays queued.

get.summary: List a workspace's assets: metadata, never the bytes
get.description: A6 (DESIGN §32.5). Name, media type, size, sha256, timestamps and the mock-plane url of every asset, beside the workspace's stored total and the two caps (per file, per workspace). The bytes are read from each asset's url on the mock plane; there is no admin-plane download. Agent-only by policy: list_assets is the caller.

put.summary: Upload (or replace) an asset: the request body is the file
put.description: A6 (DESIGN §32.5). The body is the file's bytes, RAW — not multipart, not JSON — and Content-Type is the file's media type (image/jpeg, image/webp, application/pdf, …); this is the one state-changing route whose Content-Type is not application/json, and it still requires X-CSRF-Token. A second PUT under the same name replaces the bytes and answers 200 where the first answered 201. Refused by name: an unparseable or empty type (415), a type a browser executes — text/html, application/xhtml+xml, image/svg+xml (415), a body over MOCKER_MAX_ASSET (413 asset_too_large), a workspace total over MOCKER_MAX_ASSETS_TOTAL (413 assets_quota). Bumps the workspace revision; takes no auto checkpoint (no checkpoint carries asset bytes, §32.4). The response's url is the mock-plane address the file is served at.

requestBody.description: The file's bytes, verbatim. Declare its media type in Content-Type.

200.description: Replaced an existing asset of that name.

delete.description: A6 (DESIGN §32.5). Permanent: no checkpoint carries asset bytes, and the only recovery is a new upload under the same name — which is also the repair for a bodyRef or an asset_url still naming it (neither is refused nor changed; they answer asset_missing / a 404 url until the name exists again). confirmSlug is the workspace's own slug, checked inside the delete's transaction: absent answers 400 confirm_slug_required, a mismatch 409 confirm_slug_mismatch (checked BEFORE existence, so a wrong slug learns nothing), an unknown name 404 asset_not_found. Bumps the workspace revision; no auto checkpoint.

get.summary: Export a workspace as a portable bundle (P4b)
get.description: Answers the workspace's whole configuration layer as the mockerBundle v6 document a checkpoint's config_snap holds (settings, overrides, custom endpoints, resources, decisions), decoded and key-sorted. `includeData=true` adds the entity rows of every confirmed family under `data` (the same document a checkpoint's data_snap holds); `includeSpec=true` inlines the bound spec's bytes AS UPLOADED under `spec.inline` as one JSON string, so the document imports on an installation that has never seen the spec. Assets are never carried (DESIGN §32.4). Content-Disposition names the download `<slug>.mocker.json`. Agent-only: export_workspace.

parameters.name: includeSpec
parameters.description: Inline the bound spec's bytes under `spec.inline`.

413.description: `export_too_large`: the entity rows exceed the snapshot budget; export without includeData.

get.summary: The workspace as one OpenAPI document (P7a)
get.description: Composes the bound spec's normalized document (an empty OpenAPI 3.1 skeleton when no spec is bound) with the Workspace layer over it, per DESIGN §34.4: a custom endpoint at a new shape becomes an operation, one at a base operation's canonical shape REPLACES that operation, an override's schemaPatch is written inline on the response schema, a pinned body becomes an `examples` entry, `routeOff` marks the operation `deprecated: true` rather than deleting it, and `info.version` carries `-draft.<revision>` (an earlier draft suffix is stripped first). An `overrideOn: false` row is omitted. The body is the RAW document, not an envelope: it is what a code generator, a reviewer or `import_spec` reads. `download=1` adds a Content-Disposition. Agent-only: export_openapi.

parameters.name: download
parameters.description: Add a Content-Disposition so a browser saves the document.

schema.description: An OpenAPI 3.1 document. Untyped on purpose: it is a whole specification document, and the client hands it to a viewer or back to import_spec.

post.summary: Create a workspace from a bundle (P4b)
post.description: Creates a NEW workspace from an export document (or any mockerBundle v6 document) in one transaction — the row, its configuration layer, the entity rows under `data` (for families the document also confirms), and a baseline checkpoint of kind manual labelled «импорт». The spec is resolved in order: `specId` when given (404 if unknown); the document's `spec.hash` when a spec of the same bytes is already imported; the document's `spec.inline`, imported now and deduplicated by hash; none when the document names no spec. A document naming a hash this installation lacks, with no inline copy, answers 409 `spec_not_found` with `{hash, name}` in details. `name` overrides the document's workspace name; `slug` is uniquified from the name when omitted, exactly as on create. Not idempotent. Agent-only: import_workspace.

400.description: `invalid_bundle` (the validator's own words: which entry, which field), an invalid slug, or a missing name.

409.description: `conflict` (slug taken), `spec_not_found` (details: `{hash, name}`), or `endpoint_ref_unresolved` (P7a, D6): a `$ref` in the document's endpoints[] does not resolve into the spec the import binds (details: EndpointRefConflict rows, endpointId omitted because the rows are not stored yet); no workspace is created.

post.summary: Copy a workspace inside this installation (P4b)
post.description: Creates a copy of the workspace in one transaction: the whole configuration layer, the scenarios (the active one stays active on the copy), the uploaded assets (bytes included), and — unless `includeData` is false — the entity rows of every confirmed family. The copy gets its own slug and URL, `forkedFrom` set to the source's id, and a baseline checkpoint labelled «копия воркспейса <slug>». The source is not written: no revision bump, no checkpoint. Checkpoints and traffic are not copied. `name` defaults to the source's name plus « (копия)». Not idempotent. Agent-only: fork_workspace.

409.description: `conflict`: slug taken, or the source kept changing while it was being copied.
